key_insight: HEPTv2 is an end-to-end point transformer that reconstructs charged-particle tracks directly from detector hits, avoiding graph building and auxiliary preprocessing while preserving high accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The model targets real-time track reconstruction at HL-LHC scale, offering a strong accuracy-latency-memory trade-off for high-throughput detector inference.
method: Locality-aware point encoder with locality-sensitive hashing in detector coordinate space
Sectorized track decoder that predicts complete trajectories directly from hits
Joint encoder-decoder training for end-to-end optimization without graph construction or filtering
evidence_signal: On TrackML, HEPTv2 reaches 98.6% double-majority tracking efficiency at a 0.8% fake rate with about 15 ms latency and 0.4 GB peak memory per event on an NVIDIA A100.
watch_item: Performance and scalability are demonstrated on TrackML and may depend on detector geometry, hit density, and implementation details of the locality-sensitive hashing and sector decoding pipeline.
paper_title: HEPTv2: End-to-End Efficient Point Transformer for Charged Particle Reconstruction
